{{Short description|Computational complexity class}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=March 2024}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=March 2024}}
In [[computational complexity theory]], '''LOGCFL''' is the [[complexity class]] that contains all [[decision problem]]s that can be reduced in [[logarithmic space]] to a [[context-free language]].{{r|companion}} This class is closed under complementation.{{r|companion}} It is situated between [[NL (complexity)|NL]] and [[AC (complexity)|AC<sup>1</sup>]], in the sense that it contains the former{{r|companion}} and is contained in the latter.{{r|kapron}} Problems that are [[Complete (complexity)|complete]] for LOGCFL include many problems that can be characterized by [[Directed acyclic graph|acyclic]] [[hypergraph]]s:
* evaluating acyclic [[Boolean conjunctive query|Boolean conjunctive queries]]{{r|gls}}
* checking the existence of a [[homomorphism]] between two acyclic [[relational structure]]s{{r|vk}}
* checking the existence of solutions of acyclic [[constraint satisfaction problem]]s{{r|gls}}
LOGCFL is the set of decision problems solvable by [[Nondeterministic finite automaton|nondeterministic]] auxiliary [[Pushdown automaton|pushdown automata]] in [[Space complexity|log space]] and [[Time complexity|polynomial time]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sudborough |first=I. H. |date=July 1978 |title=On the Tape Complexity of Deterministic Context-Free Languages |url=https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/322077.322083 |journal=Journal of the ACM |language=en |volume=25 |issue=3 |pages=405–414 |doi=10.1145/322077.322083 |issn=0004-5411|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
